_about: Key places on the map: 3 to 5 per region, only places an official source names, each line one idea, all backed by the cites (owner card 18 Oct 2026, style B name chips). Shown while one of the listed places is selected. Positions are OpenStreetMap points (data/SOURCES.md, Map flags).

flags.name: Haro
lines: Rioja's westernmost town.
A French firm in its station quarter hired a champagne maker from Reims in 1890.

flags.name: Sierra de Cantabria
lines: The mountains on the northern side.
They shelter Rioja Alta, and Rioja Alavesa even more.

flags.name: Ebro
lines: The vineyards lie on both banks of the river.
Alluvial soils near the rivers make up half the land.

flags.name: Alfaro
lines: Rioja's easternmost town, 100 km from Haro.

flags.name: Jerez de la Frontera
lines: One of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda
lines: One of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.
Manzanilla has its own DO named after it.

flags.name: El Puerto de Santa María
lines: The third of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Guadalete
lines: The river is the southern edge of the area where Sherry is aged.

flags.name: Chipiona
lines: Moscatel may also be aged here, and in Chiclana.

flags.name: Bakio
lines: One of the places where txakoli survived into the 20th century.

flags.name: Bilbao
lines: A 15th-century visitor marvelled at the vines around the city.

flags.name: Lekeitio
lines: Its ordinances of 1338 exempted from tax the timber used to train vines.

flags.name: Ibaizabal
lines: With the Butrón, it gives its name to one of the two main valleys.

flags.name: Getaria
lines: In the 19th century it kept 35 ha of vines in sheltered spots.

flags.name: Zarautz
lines: In the 19th century it kept 4 ha of vines, under Santa Bárbara.

flags.name: Aia
lines: One of the three municipalities the DO began with.

flags.name: Donostia / San Sebastián
lines: A charter granted to the city in 1180 already mentions vines.

flags.name: Amurrio
lines: One of the places where txakoli was common practice by the 9th century.

flags.name: Laudio / Llodio
lines: A gift of vineyards to the lost monastery of San Víctor is recorded in its Gardea quarter.

flags.name: Artziniega
lines: Vines are recorded at Retes de Tudela in 864.

flags.name: Ayala / Aiara
lines: Vines were grown for wine in the Tierra de Ayala in 964.

flags.name: Cangas del Narcea
lines: One of the seven municipalities of the area.

flags.name: Narcea
lines: With the Navia, it is one of the two main rivers of the area.

flags.name: Monasterio de Corias
lines: The vine spread widely after this Benedictine monastery was founded in the early 11th century.

flags.name: Cambados
lines: A municipality of the Val do Salnés subzone.

flags.name: Salvaterra de Miño
lines: A municipality of the Condado do Tea subzone.

flags.name: Soutomaior
lines: Its municipality forms the Soutomaior subzone.

flags.name: Padrón
lines: A municipality of the Ribeira do Ulla subzone.

flags.name: Portomarín
lines: The area runs from here to A Peroxa.

flags.name: A Peroxa
lines: The area runs from Portomarín to here.

flags.name: Quiroga
lines: The area runs from Os Peares to here.

flags.name: Cañón del Sil
lines: The Sil and the Miño flow through steep canyons towards their meeting.
The canyons and the religious buildings gave the area its name, which goes back to the 12th century.

flags.name: O Barco de Valdeorras
lines: Clay-limestone soils lie in the north of the area, here and in Rubiá.

flags.name: A Rúa
lines: Loose granite soils lie here, in Petín and in Larouco.

flags.name: Sil
lines: The river crosses the area from east to west.
Its left bank is steep and its right bank gentler.

flags.name: Ribadavia
lines: Its municipal ordinances of 1579 set out where vines could be grown.

flags.name: Carballeda de Avia
lines: One of the nine municipalities listed whole for the area.

flags.name: Pontevedra
lines: The main port for shipping the wine by sea.

flags.name: Verín
lines: Its parishes of Verín and Vilamaior do Val belong to the Monterrei valley subzone.

flags.name: Oímbra
lines: Its parishes of Oímbra, Rabal and San Cibrao belong to the Monterrei valley subzone.

flags.name: Vilardevós
lines: The whole municipality is in the Monterrei slope subzone.

flags.name: Monterrei
lines: The wines of the Monterrei valley rivalled those of Porto.
